full_text:
**Verdict: KNOWN.** The core rule is the voter model on a sparse network. The REWIRE variant is the coevolving (adaptive) voter model. My confidence is medium-high for the core rule and medium for the Kuramoto and CYCLE hybrids.

**1. Model family**
- `N kN=4 | ALWAYS -> COPY_RAND p=0.2` means each node, with probability 0.2, copies the state of a randomly chosen neighbour in a degree-~4 graph. That is the standard pull voter model. My search turned up this description: an individual "imports" its state from a randomly chosen neighbor.
- `N.REWIRE(p=0.003); N.COPY(p=0.3)` is copying plus slow link rewiring. That is the coevolving voter model: The coevolving voter model consists of two dynamical processes: copying and rewiring.
- `N.KURA(K); N.COPY(p)` and `N.CYCLE; N.COPY(p=1.0)` are hybrids of a phase-oscillator step with voter copying. I did not find a canonical model for these. The closest related work I found treats consensus as synchronisation in a Kuramoto-type opinion model (consensus as a peculiar kind of synchronization (frequency locking)). That is a conceptual link, not the same system.

**2. The specific behaviours**
- **Consensus (n_giant, n_consensus_gain).** Voter dynamics on finite connected graphs reach consensus. One source states that the voter algorithm converges to a network wide consensus in finite networks. Consensus time depends on network structure: the average time TN to reach consensus for a network of N nodes with an uncorrelated degree distribution scales as N mu1 2/mu2. This is from Sood, Antal & Redner, PRE 77, 041121 (2008), "Voter models on heterogeneous networks".
- **Duality with coalescing random walks.** The duality relationship between voter models and "coalescing RWs" makes analysis of RWs a powerful approach for calculating consensus probability and mean consensus time. This is in the review "Random walks and diffusion on networks" (arXiv:1612.03281).
- **Multiple components, with a giant component alongside them (n_components).** This is the fragmentation behaviour of rewiring voter models. Holme & Newman (PRE 74, 056108, 2006) found a transition between a giant community and many small ones, and Durrett et al. describe it: When α = 1, only rewiring steps occur, so once all of the M edges have been touched, the graph has been disconnected into G components.
  - Vazquez, Eguíluz & San Miguel (PRL 100, 108702, 2008) identified a "generic absorbing transition" with an active phase and a frozen phase.
  - With rewiring this slow (p=0.003 against copying at 0.3), I would expect consensus before fragmentation. I did not test that.
- **Review sources.**
  - Adaptive voter models: "Modeling complex systems with adaptive networks" (arXiv:1301.2561) says The simplest and best-understood model exhibiting the fragmentation transition is the adaptive voter model.
  - Coevolving voter models: arXiv:2311.05882 / Frontiers in Complex Systems 2023 is a review of coevolving nonlinear voter models.
- **Oscillation (n_oscillation, 0.808).** I did not find a source for oscillation in plain voter dynamics. It is probably finite-size fluctuation of the state densities, or a metric artefact. In the KURA variants the oscillation is probably just the Kuramoto phases. I could not verify this, and it is the weakest part of my conclusion.

**3. Why the fingerprint looks atypical**
The test passes (consensus gain is high), but the profile differs from textbook voter-model output. That is expected for two reasons. The 49 programs mix several mechanisms, and a metric suite designed for other behaviours will pick up side effects such as component counts and degree variation. A mixed profile does not on its own indicate a new phenomenon.

**Caveats**
- The earliest clear source is Clifford & Sudbury (1973) and Holley & Liggett (1975), cited from memory. My searches did not return those papers, so I have not verified them. The earliest sources I verified are Holme & Newman 2006 and Vazquez et al. 2008, which I saw only in the reference lists of the papers above.
- I did not find a source for the exact Kuramoto-plus-copy and cycle-plus-copy hybrids. If those are the interesting part, they could be KNOWN-VARIANT or LITERATURE-SILENT. I did not run a dedicated search for them, so I cannot call them literature-silent.
